candidate_result_row.claim: At the production-measured marginal rows/game r = 18.5249 and its drift-based lower bound r_lo = 16.9968, NUM_GAMES_PER_CYCLE = 1500 -- with every other knob of the 2026-09-04 set unchanged (shuffle threads 8, epoch 20000, reuse 8, SWA 10000, batch 128, MINROWS 25000, cap 100000, taper 50000, KEEPROWS 120000, EPOCHS_PER_EXPORT 5 passed as both -epochs-per-export and -max-epochs-this-instance, --cpus-per-task 32 at numGameThreads 18) -- satisfies every constraint train.py and shuffle.py impose, at BOTH rates. Specifically: a cycle produces 27787 new rows (25495 at r_lo) against the 24000-row freshness floor of 1.2*samples_per_epoch, restoring the tolerance that 18525 rows at 1000 games violated by 22.8 %; the bucket gain 222299 (203962) clears 0.99*E by 11.1x (10.2x); epochs_per_export stays 5 because the gain clears cap_eff = max(cap,E) = 100000 by 2.2x, so the knob that fixes it is MAX_TRAIN_SAMPLES_PER_CYCLE, not the game count; realised reuse falls from 5.40 to 3.60 (3.92 at r_lo) against the cap of 8; keep 120000 > cap 100000 and holds a whole cycle's draw; the shuffle window holds at least one epoch in every cycle including the first (worst case 195 batches against 156); the worst stage thread count is 28 projected and 24 measured against 32 declared, and is independent of the game count because -max-games-total is a loop bound, not a concurrency knob; the projected cycle is 0.392 h so 182 whole cycles fit one 2-23:30:00 link; and the projection writes 15.89 MiB per cycle monotonic, 23.37 GiB after a full link against the 500 GiB cap. THREE THINGS ARE NOT CLAIMED. (i) No cycle has executed at 1500 games -- the evidence is a derivation over production measurements plus an executed arithmetic check, not a measurement of the loop at this value. (ii) The bound is a HORIZON, not a resting point: at the measured -0.1528 rows/game per accepted net the marginal reaches 16.0, where T1 fails again at 1500, after ~16.5 further accepted nets (~52 cycles). 1500 buys a monitored horizon of about ten accepted nets. (iii) SHUFFLE_MINROWS 25000 is re-asserted but is not TESTED by link 2: it binds only a cycle-1 random bootstrap, and link 2 resumes a mature window pinned at SHUFFLE_KEEPROWS = 120000 rows, five times min_rows.

candidate_result_row._validator_decision_point: Three places to attack. (1) THE LOWER BOUND. It is the only number in the derivation that is a modelling choice rather than an aggregate, and it is what makes 1412 the binding inequality rather than 1296. A refuter should ask whether ten accepted nets is the right horizon, whether the nine-net window is the right fit (all thirteen complete real nets would give a much steeper slope because they span the one-time moves/game collapse), and whether excluding the newest directory as incomplete is right -- the two snapshots of the SAME 18035 rows at 1136 and 1040 games are the argument, and they are in status_log.txt read 4 and rows_per_game.txt respectively. (2) THE MARGINAL WINDOW. Three net directories is 8000 games; two would give 18.397 and four 18.643, so the choice moves r by 1.3 % and does not move the knob -- but the validator should confirm that on the file. (3) WHETHER 1500 IS THE RIGHT RESPONSE AT ALL. It restores T1 for about ten accepted nets and costs ~50 % more selfplay wall per cycle (652 s -> 978 s at the measured 5520 games/h). Lowering NUM_TRAIN_SAMPLES_PER_EPOCH would restore the same ratio for free, at the cost of the metrics floor (E >= 100*batch = 12800, so E could fall to 12800 and 1.2*E to 15360, which 1000 games at the marginal 18.525 clears with +20 %). The human fixed the value; the alternative is recorded here because scale_data_window owns it and should see it.
